claims.subject: telos/raw-data-and-projections
claims.author: did:key:zDnaebVRiiKts4HkYSXknYdTZgmWgwRhGuD8LFXimVqaeJZFc
claims.text: Raw attested data is retained in full and never collapsed in the store. Every simplification -- identity, status, confidence, tension, ordering -- is a determined projection computed on demand over that raw data, parameterised by a base the viewer chooses, and therefore swappable: a different base over the same claims yields a different, equally valid view. SPEC section 4.3 states this for identity (M(A,B) as a witness-retaining path-space enriched over the trust structure, so the same SameAs set under a different trust base gives a different identity); the disposable SQLite index, the state fold's poset, and decategorification-only-at-render are the same principle in other places. A field holding a computed value is the failure mode: it asserts an output of the fold as if it were input, and it forecloses every other projection.

claims.subject: telos/raw-data-and-projections
claims.author: did:key:zDnaebVRiiKts4HkYSXknYdTZgmWgwRhGuD8LFXimVqaeJZFc
claims.text:
THIS TELOS DECLARES NO WITNESSES, DELIBERATELY. Not an oversight, and not work waiting to be done -- recorded here so a later session reads the reason instead of re-deriving it or, worse, closing the gap with a witness that cannot fail.

In its plain reading this is a MAINTENANCE telos: raw data retained and never collapsed is a property that must keep holding, and the day after the first cache lands is when it is under load. day cannot express that today. `assess telos` is cumulative by design and a claim probe ignores --scope by design, so any witness available now would report met forever after the first pass -- day#138's failure, and what day#86 calls worse than leaving a telos unwitnessed. telos/cross-harness-maintained hit the same wall and was deliberately left undeclared; it is filed as day#171, a design question about the telos model rather than a missing probe.

What the witness interview produced instead is telos/raw-data-and-projections-attained, which asks whether the machinery that makes this principle CHECKABLE has been built: a specification of the read/write surface, every stored value declared raw or derived, and a conformance test binding that declaration to the code under the migration matrix's own rule -- a stored value with no committed row is an error, not a pass. That half is attainment, reports met forever once reached, and is witnessed by `spec-conformance`, which reports absent today because the test does not exist yet.

So the division of labour is: day witnesses the attainment, CI enforces the maintenance. `day assess telos raw-data-and-projections` continuing to say this telos declares no witnesses is the honest reading, not a gap to close.
